disease.name: Jassids
disease.severity_index: Can cause up to 30–50% yield loss if not managed

environmental_factors.soil_conditions: High moisture in the soil encourages pest infestation

disease.region_specific_information: Higher infestations occur in regions with frequent rainfall and dense cropping.

early_stage: Yellowing and curling of leaf margins
mid_stage: Heavy infestation leads to burnt appearance of leaves (Hopper Burn)
advanced_stage: Reduced chlorophyll, leading to poor photosynthesis
Can lead to up to 30–50% yield loss if not managed

crop_rotation: Intercropping with sorghum/millet reduces pest occurrence
soil_seed_treatment: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70 WS @ 5 g/kg seed reduces early-stage attacks

cultural_practices: Intercropping with sorghum/millet reduces pest occurrence
Using yellow sticky traps to monitor adult populations
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizers as they promote pest multiplication
Ensure well-drained soil to reduce moisture-loving insect population
biological_control: Release of Chrysoperla carnea (Green Lacewing) as a natural predator
Spraying Neem Oil @ 5 ml/liter water to deter infestation
